_note: Weekly editorial. Update every week: "moving" = 3-4 stories moving markets, "trending" = 4 stocks explained. Owners, politician and insider activity are added automatically from the data.

moving.title: AI stocks lead a sell-off
moving.text: The Nasdaq fell 2.1% on Friday and 4.5% for the week, ending a four-week winning streak. Chip, memory and AI-infrastructure stocks led the decline as investors questioned how AI spending gets financed.

moving.title: Hot inflation, higher yields
moving.text: Hotter-than-expected CPI and PPI readings pushed the 10-year Treasury yield above 5%. Futures markets price a high chance of a Fed rate hike by December.

moving.title: Oil back above $100
moving.text: WTI crude rose 3.4% to about $101 a barrel, and Brent to about $110, on Middle East supply risks. Energy was the best-performing sector.

trending.title: CoreWeave slides on AI-debt worries
trending.happened: CoreWeave fell about 12% on Friday, its second big drop in three days, as investors focused on the AI cloud provider’s roughly $50 billion of debt.
trending.means: Companies that borrow to build AI data centres now trade like rate-sensitive stocks. With 10-year yields above 5%, financing costs matter as much as demand. Expect volatility until earnings show cash flow catching up with spending.
trending.note: David Tepper’s Appaloosa opened a new position in Q2 2026, before this sell-off.

trending.title: Meta falls 4% ahead of earnings
trending.happened: Meta dropped nearly 4% on Friday as the AI sell-off hit the biggest spenders on AI infrastructure.
trending.means: Upcoming Big Tech earnings must show AI investment turning into revenue and cash flow. Meta’s ad business funds its spending, which separates it from borrowers, but the market wants proof.
trending.note: One of the most widely held stocks among our super investors.

trending.title: Netflix reports earnings on 20 October
trending.happened: Netflix reports third-quarter results on Tuesday, 20 October, at the start of a heavy week of earnings.
trending.means: Subscriber growth, ad-tier revenue and margins will set the tone. A streaming business is less exposed to AI financing fears, which may help it stand out in a jittery tape.
trending.note: Bill Ackman’s Pershing Square opened a new position worth about $934 million in Q2 2026.

trending.title: Oil above $100 lifts energy stocks
trending.happened: Energy was the best sector on Friday (up about 2.5%) as WTI crude climbed above $101 a barrel on Middle East supply risks.
trending.means: Producers like Occidental earn much more cash at these prices, which supports buybacks and debt paydown. The risk is that oil prices fall back quickly if supply eases.
trending.note: Berkshire Hathaway owns about 265 million Occidental shares, one of its largest positions.
